messages.subject: Storing output from handle_hover() or handle_click()
messages.subject_clean: Storing output from handle_hover() or handle_click()
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,
I was just wondering if there would be a way of storing the output printed to the console from overing over the graph, ideally i am hoping to use this to link two plots in a shiny app via a key

Example code:

library(ggvis)
mtcars$id <- seq_len(nrow(mtcars))

hoveron<-function(data,...){
  testval<-str(data)
}

mtcars %>% ggvis(~mpg, ~wt,key:=~id) %>% layer_points() %>%
  handle_hover(hoveron)

hoping to be able to store the id value of the point which is being hovered over in testval.

Many thanks!

messages.subject: Can't get interactive zooming to work with ggvis
messages.subject_clean: Can't get interactive zooming to work with ggvis
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm trying to get interactive zooming to work in ggvis, more in particular zooming using a brush. Judging from https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/143 I thought this should work.

I have the following shiny and ggvis code (is fully reproducible):

## ui.R
library(ggvis)

shinyUI(fluidRow(
  uiOutput('ui_plot1'),
  ggvisOutput("graph_plot1")
))

## server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  domains <- reactiveValues(x = c(NA, NA), y = c(NA, NA))

  zoom_brush = function(items, session, page_loc, plot_loc, ...) {
    domains$x = c(200, 400)
  }

  plot = reactive({
    mtcars %>%
      ggvis(~disp, ~mpg) %>%
      layer_points() %>%
      scale_numeric('x', domain = domains$x, clamp = TRUE) %>%
      handle_brush(zoom_brush)
  }) %>% bind_shiny('graph_plot1', 'ui_plot1')
})

So, as soon as a brush is drawn, the ranges reactive is changed, which in turn changes the domain of the x `scale_numeric`. If still have the following challenges:

- Inside `zoom_brush` I get the coordinates of the brush, but in the pixel coordinate system of the plot not the domain coordinate system. How can I translate the pixels to the domain scale? In d3 I can simply use the range to scale transform functions, but I don't see how these are available in ggvis (via vega).
- The handle_brush function only supports setting a `on_move` event handler. In this case I only want to trigger the zoom if the brush finishes, so the onmouseup event in the context of the brush. I fear that this is simply not possible right now?
- Only when I set clamp = TRUE do I get an effective zoom. In not, the points outiside the domain are still shown and only the axes are set to the new domain. Is there an easy fix for this? Or should I make the dataset a reactive, and subset it based on the domain that was set by the brush?

In general, how far is ggvis in being ready for production? And are there plans to extend the functionality of ggvis to make it closer to d3 in terms of flexibility? Or should I focus on using `ggplot2` witht the brushes of shiny (which I got working already)?

Thanks for any feedback!
Paul

messages.subject: Re: Treatment of NA in time series with layer_lines()
messages.subject_clean: Treatment of NA in time series with layer_lines()
messages.body_plain:
Possibly too late, but to get rid of the lines going back to the y axis, have you tried setting the renderer to Canvas

On Wednesday, April 1, 2015 at 4:24:49 AM UTC+11, Claymore Marshall wrote:
> You could do this trick to get around the problem of the "y-axis" values having NA's (make both the x and y values NA, not just one of them):
>
> library(ggvis)
>
> na_eg <- data.frame(
>     period = 1:20,
>     value = c(2, 1, rep(NA, 8), rnorm(10) + 1:10)
> )
>
>
> na_eg[is.na <http://is.na>(na_eg$value), "period"] <- NA
>
> na_eg2 <- na_eg[!is.na <http://is.na>(na_eg$value),]
>
> na_eg2 %>%
>     ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%
>     layer_lines() %>% layer_points()
>
> Note in the above example that I added layer_points just to show that the line moves from the second point to the 10th point without plotting any points in between.
>
> An aside, but when I do this (for the above example)
>
> na_eg %>%
>     ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%
>     layer_lines() %>% layer_points()
>
> I get the line draw back to the y-axis strangely (see screenshot attached).  Looks like a bug.
>
>
>
>
>
> On Saturday, March 28, 2015 at 4:58:43 PM UTC-4, Matt Gibbs wrote:
> > Did anyone find a solution to this? I have found the same problem, but the na values are in the middle of the data, so the filling with the maximum values are even more obvious, and more difficult to fix (could do na.interp I guess, but that could be missleading).
> >
> > I have found that if the renderer is set to canvas rather than SVG the plot will interpolate rather than just showing the maximum. Either by clicking in the browser, or adding this to the ggvis() command:
> > %>% set_options(renderer="canvas")
> >
> > Ideally, the plot would show a gap when there is no data.
> >
> > On Sunday, February 8, 2015 at 7:03:29 PM UTC+10:30, Peter Ellis wrote:
> > > In my line of work I often have  a time series that begins with a bunch of NAs before real values come in.  I often want the plot to cover the whole period including the NAs, but ggvis seems to default to plotting the NA values at the maximum value or (oddly) just slightly higher than the maximum value.  This is rarely the desired behaviour eg see below.  I could probably contrive a workaround (remove the NA data altogether, and then force the x axis still to start at the beginning of the original data), but is there a simpler way of dealing with this?
> > >
> > >
> > > library(ggvis)
> > >
> > > na_eg <- data.frame(
> > >    period = 1:20,
> > >    value = c(rep(NA, 10), rnorm(10) + 1:10)
> > >    )
> > >
> > > na_eg %>%
> > >    ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%
> > >    layer_lines()
> > >
> > >  <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-vctMRmJn_GQ/VNce4cCAf6I/AAAAAAAAAJ8/a8dC9anKoYo/s1600/NA%2Beg.png>
> > >
